checks: Cold review started from the frozen JSON. Then checked archived candidate 44be6cdd33cc2f74 at 27bf01c; its exact SHA-256 is 8f00cb30b67687283f9c46c4eb924332b46cd5bf6442983f93d3132185cf1ce6. Sections 1–8 and (1)–(12) support the normalized claim. The normalization explicitly proves Hausdorff continuity and uses an accepted isolation theorem for the archive's finite-tilt argument at collapse.

An integer base translation and possible reflection send the chosen endpoint to −1 and the other endpoint to 1 even when their lengths agree. Subtracting the interpolating affine height and possibly reflecting heights preserves length, lattice points, and every halfspace trace mass. The midpoint inclusion is necessary and sufficient for the lifted hull's three exact fibers; at base zero equal endpoint weights reduce to that inclusion, even at a=0. The b-segment and any point at another base give a nondegenerate triangle.

The initial lifted hull H lies in the original body C. By convexity, H is contained in each (1−t)C+tH, which is contained in C; hence all integer fibers and every cap mass and candidate point remain fixed even if the original projection extends beyond [−1,1].

For a>0 the accepted exact closed-halfspace profile gives Q=max(b/2,F) and F≥(U+a)/2>a/2. Thus the chosen interval is never deepest while positive. Increasing s keeps midpoint compatibility and gives nonincreasing D by the fixed-length profile; the raw F slopes in s are 0, −1/2, 0 with matching values at both joins. Substituting s=U/2−(a+b)/4 gives the contact seams U=b and U=b+2a with common raw values b/2+a and (b+3a)/2 respectively.

On contact the only possible positive tie is U=b−2a, which is compatible exactly when 5a≤b. If F≤b/2, increasing U to that value keeps raw maximum b/2 and weakly increases W; the existing-tie case is a constant piece. If F>b/2, shrinking a at fixed U improves compatibility. For W=a+b+U, the independently differentiated numerators W²∂aD are b+U/2, 3(b+U)/4 and b/2 on the three middle-dominant branches. At U=b the first two derivatives coincide; at the interior a-seam a*=(U−b)/2>0 the two one-sided numerators are b/2 and 3(b+U)/4, both positive, with the same value of D. If U<b, the tie a=(b−U)/2 lies strictly below the starting a and is reached first; if U≥b no positive tie can occur.

The fixed-U shrink must stop at a positive tie: continuation into endpoint dominance would have ∂aD=−b/(2W²). The prescribed tie path instead keeps U=b−2a, s=(b−5a)/4 and W=2b−a; 5a≤b persists and both deepest raw values remain b/2. Its derivative in a is b/[2(2b−a)²]>0, so decreasing a decreases D to 1/4.

At collapse the closed halfspace z≤−1 contains the singleton and no positive mass, giving that point depth zero. For a point (0,x), either intrinsic closed interval cap is lifted by ±(X−x)−Rz≥0; for a point (1,x) use ±(X−x)+R(z−1)≥0. For sufficiently large finite R the other positive interval is excluded; any captured singleton contributes zero. Conversely every containing closed ambient cap captures at least intrinsic depth in its own interval. This also directly verifies the use of 2acc8bc803acf1c0 and the maxima U/2 and b/2 for both remaining positive fibers.

If U>b is fixed at collapse, the last positive contact branch tends to U/2; if U=b, the first/second common branch tends to b/2. Along the tie route both raw maxima stay b/2 until a=0 and the collapsed U=b profile gives the same value. Since W stays at least b>0, the normalized limits agree with D=U/[2(U+b)]. Reducing U≥b to b retains compatibility and has ∂UD=b/[2(U+b)²]>0, with exact terminal value 1/4.

The support functions vary affinely and uniformly on unit directions on the optional Minkowski piece. On all later pieces, same-weight convex combinations in the hulls of the six corresponding lifted endpoints give a Hausdorff bound by their maximum displacement, including when two coincide. Parameters match at all joins, the fixed affine inverse is Lipschitz, and b is fixed throughout. After the Minkowski and translation pieces, each route uses at most two additional affine-endpoint pieces; a constant piece can be omitted. D is continuous at every join and seam by the checked formulas.

As a supplementary exact-arithmetic check, compared the contact formula to the translated profile and cross-multiplied the depth ratios along rational grid paths for 1,173 compatible positive triples, covering initial ties, endpoint dominance, descent to positive tie, collapse at U=b, and collapse at U>b. All checked points remained compatible and reached the stated terminal ratio. The symbolic checks establish the full real-parameter claim.

summary: The frozen proof constructs the claimed path from every starting body, including equal initial endpoint lengths, an existing positive tie, and collapse with or without a previous positive tie. The four-piece bound and both continuities hold. The full monotone path from arbitrary initial data is distinct from the accepted static depth formula, fixed-ratio optimization and exposed-fiber depth formula.
